_comment: AI neural network and PPO hyperparameters. All tunable constants live here, not hardcoded - mirrors physics.json/attributes.json pattern.

observation._comment_sim_dt_s: Physics tick size. Default 0.0333 (30Hz). Increase for faster training: 0.05=20Hz (~1.5x), 0.067=15Hz (~2x). UI ignores this and always uses 30Hz.
observation._comment_time: Use log1p normalization for time_remaining to spread out the low end (see ai_design_doc.md section 7.5)

network._comment: Shared-trunk actor/critic (Option A from section 9.4). Switch to separate trunk if value loss destabilises policy.

ppo._comment_gamma: Discount factor: how much future rewards are worth vs immediate ones. Think of it as 'I care about a reward in N steps at gamma^N of its face value'. 0.99 = reward 100 steps away is worth 37% of today's reward. 0.995 = same reward is still worth 61%. Typical range: 0.95–0.999. We use 0.995 because episodes are long (~120s, ~170 decision steps) and the terminal reward (+5) is the main signal — too low and the agent gives up on distant goals, too high and variance explodes. Raise toward 0.999 if the agent seems short-sighted; lower toward 0.99 if training is unstable.
ppo._comment_lam: GAE lambda: controls the bias/variance tradeoff in advantage estimation. lam=1.0 is pure Monte Carlo (low bias, high variance — noisy but unbiased). lam=0.0 is pure TD(0) (high bias, low variance — smooth but wrong). Typical range: 0.9–0.99. We use 0.97 as a standard middle ground. Lower (e.g. 0.9) if gradients are noisy and training oscillates; raise (e.g. 0.99) if the agent seems to discount future steps too aggressively.
ppo._comment_clip_range: PPO clipping: the policy ratio (new_prob / old_prob) is clamped to [1-clip, 1+clip] = [0.95, 1.05] here. This stops a single update from changing the policy too drastically — the gradient is zeroed for any sample where the ratio goes outside the band. Typical value is 0.2; we use 0.05 (very conservative) because the KL was spiking to 0.4+ with 0.1, causing early-stop after just 2 minibatches. Lower clip = more conservative updates, more minibatches get through. If you see 25+ minibatches per rollout and training is slow, try raising to 0.1.
ppo._comment_vf_coef: Value function loss coefficient: scales how hard the critic trains relative to the actor. total_loss = policy_loss + vf_coef*value_loss - ent_coef*entropy. Typical: 0.5. Raise if the value estimates are wildly off (large RMSE vs returns std); lower if value gradients seem to destabilise the policy (rare).
ppo._comment_ent_coef: Entropy bonus: rewards the policy for being uncertain/exploratory. Higher = more random behaviour, harder to converge to a good strategy but less likely to get stuck in local optima. Typical range: 0.0–0.1. We use 0.1 (fairly high) because the agent needs to explore a large action space and sprint/kick/tackle heads that start at ~50% probability. Lower toward 0.01 later in training once the policy has converged to sensible behaviour.
ppo._comment_max_grad_norm: Gradient clipping: if the total gradient vector has magnitude > this, all gradients are scaled down proportionally. Acts as a safety valve against catastrophic updates from rare high-loss samples. 0.5 is standard for PPO. Raise to 1.0 if gradients feel too constrained (loss barely moves per step); lower to 0.3 if you see sudden policy collapses. Check the 'g=' value in the per-rollout log — if it's consistently hitting 0.5 exactly, you're clipping every update.
ppo._comment_learning_rate: Step size for Adam optimiser. Typical PPO LR is 3e-4, but we use 5e-6 because (a) augmentation multiplies the effective batch by 12x meaning each gradient step sees more signal, and (b) the BC-pretrained policy is already near a good point so large steps would destroy it. Raise to 1e-5 if training feels too slow; lower to 1e-6 if the policy collapses after pretraining.
ppo._comment_target_kl: Per-minibatch early-stop threshold. KL divergence measures how much the policy distribution has changed since the rollout was collected — KL=0 means no change, KL=0.4 means fairly significant shift. When any minibatch's KL exceeds this, the entire epoch loop stops early. Typical value is 0.01–0.05; we use 0.4 (very permissive) because we want to see how many minibatches naturally get through. The real constraint is clip_range=0.05. LOWER this (e.g. 0.1) to make early-stop fire sooner and protect the policy more aggressively — you'll see fewer minibatches per rollout but more stable training. RAISE it if you want to see the full picture of how the policy changes per rollout.
ppo._comment_ent_dir_weight: Weight applied to continuous direction heads (move_dir, kick_dir) in the entropy bonus. The direction heads output a Gaussian distribution; their raw entropy is much larger in scale than a Bernoulli head. 1.0 = equal weight = direction entropy dominates the bonus and the Bernoulli heads (shoot, sprint etc.) get almost no exploration pressure. 0.05 = direction entropy contributes only 5% — Bernoulli heads drive exploration. Lower toward 0.01 if the agent spins randomly (too much directional noise); raise toward 0.2 if kicks/passes cluster on one angle.
ppo._comment_augment: Slot permutations per geometric flip variant. Total batch multiplier = 4 * n. Use 1 for 4x (flips only), 3 for 12x, 0 to disable. See ai/obs/augment.py.
ppo._comment: Standard PPO defaults from CleanRL-style reference implementations. Tune empirically.

curriculum._comment_todo: TODO: implement and wire up: rng_reduction_start/end (randomisation annealing over training), pitch_standard_fraction (fraction of episodes on standard pitch), pitch_min_scale / goal_min_scale (curriculum pitch scaling). Currently not read by any code.
curriculum._comment_phase1_opponent: phase1 training opponent split: rules_prob + immobile_prob must be <=1; remainder is neural (secondary player). phase1_demo_opponent_rules_prob is the default for record_demonstrations --opponent-rules-prob.
curriculum._comment_secondary_weight: Importance weight applied to secondary (opponent) player transitions in the PPO loss. 1.0 = equal weight, 0.5 = half weight, 0.0 = ignore secondary transitions.

bc._comment: Behavioural cloning from rules-based AI. Set pretrain_steps=0 to skip pre-training. Set aux_coeff_start=0.0 to disable the PPO auxiliary BC loss.
bc._comment_aux: aux_coeff anneals linearly from start to end over aux_coeff_anneal_fraction of training (e.g. 0.3 = done by 30% of steps). The BC loss is computed on decision Bernoulli heads and execution move_direction.
bc._comment_frozen_layers: Layers frozen (requires_grad=False) during value head warm-up. -1=all non-value layers (encoders + full trunk). 0=nothing frozen (gradients flow freely through trunk). 1=encoders only. 2=encoders + trunk layer 1. 3=encoders + full trunk (same as -1). Default -1 matches prior behaviour.
bc._comment_value: After BC pre-training, run value-only MSE warm-up so the critic is near the true return scale before PPO starts. Set value_pretrain_steps=0 to skip.
bc._comment_demo_sample: Time between timed observation samples during demonstration recording. Kick2 and tackles are always recorded regardless.

ema._comment: EMA smoothing for attack/defence weighting (section 2.7). alpha close to 1 = slow change, further from 1 = fast change.

phase1._comment_loss_terminal: Penalty applied when the opponent reaches the trainee's box with possession (trainee loses). Should be negative and less than box_possession_terminal in magnitude.
phase1._comment_loss_of_possession: Small penalty per step the trainee loses the ball to the opponent. Creates symmetric signal with gain_possession_bonus.
phase1._comment_timeout_penalty: Penalty if the episode times out (no resolution). Makes timeouts clearly worse than active play.
phase1._comment_proximity_bonus: On timeout only: bonus for how close the ball was to the opponent box. scale * max(0, 1 - dist/30m). Max = scale at box edge. Rewards making progress even when not winning.
phase1._comment_speed_bonus: Bonus for finishing fast: scale * time_remaining_fraction * min(start_ball_to_box_dist/30m, 1.5). Max bonus = 3.0 (instant finish, ball 45m+ from box). Set to 0.0 to disable.

phase1_scenario._comment_opponent_dist: Constrain opponent placement distance from trainee. Both default to unconstrained. E.g. min=5, max=20 keeps opponent nearby but not on top.
